chunks: Yet, my Lord may haply give me a garden better than yours, and He may send a thunder-bolt, from the skies and in the morning it will be a barren plain;
ai.seo_question: What does the word 'Husban' mean in the context of the garden's destruction in Surah Al-Kahf?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the wealthy man's arrogant reliance on material wealth, contrasting it with the spiritual poverty of those who trust in divine provision. The term 'husban' is interpreted by scholars like Al-Tabarsi as a specific divine punishment or calamity, serving as a warning against the transient nature of worldly assets compared to eternal spiritual rewards.
